wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: Explosions hit Qeshm Island and Bandar Lengeh in what US officials describe as US strikes, a day after Trump answered "no" on striking Iran after the midterms and as a Qatari delegation headed to Tehran. Tehran then set five conditions for any regional security deal, led by sovereignty over Hormuz, after three days of Doha talks ended without one.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: With Hormuz traffic at stake, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said 2 tankers hit mines in the strait, and OPEC+ held Saudi Arabia's December quota rather than add supply. The price slid when Trump gave Iran more time and Tehran offered a two-day Hormuz reopening, then rebounded after the Qeshm strikes.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: Over 30 attacks hit ships near Hormuz in October, and the IRGC halted two tankers in the strait, putting a war premium into crude worldwide. Hopes for Iran diplomacy knocked oil sharply lower at the start of November, until US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, which sits on the Strait of Hormuz, undid the discount a day later.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: Strikes cut Iran's gas capacity by a fifth and European gas passed €100 per megawatt hour, its highest since 2022. Qatar, usually a seller, signed two deals to buy US liquefied natural gas: up to 4 million tons a year, then up to 3 million tonnes through QatarEnergy. That export demand is what reaches this price.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: Ukraine's Black Sea grain route is still broken: Zelensky says Turkey will help restore the corridor, and Rubio sees growing interest in a limited Black Sea ceasefire. In Pakistan the first imported cargo, 51,000 tonnes, berthed in Karachi and wheat fell Rs10 a kilo, yet chapati still costs Rs20.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: Chinese buyers paid a record $200-plus a ton above London prices, a premium driven by AI demand, while Mysteel sees China's smelters cutting fourth-quarter refined output. The metal has since traded with AI stocks: it fell in a renewed selloff and held below $14,000 on US midterm risks.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: The Fed held rates, but markets now fully price a December hike, and Warsh's muddled messaging revived doubts about Fed credibility. Rising yields mean falling bond prices: Bank of America's unrealized bond losses rose to $109 billion. AI doubts briefly pulled yields down as money ran to the yen.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: The decline ran alongside a bond-market squeeze: Treasury yields climbed far enough to lift Bank of America's unrealized bond losses to $109 billion, and the Fed left interest rates unchanged despite inflation, offering no relief on borrowing costs.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The fall ran through weeks in which the cost of AI came into view. Anthropic's listing filing showed it lost $80.7 billion on $16.3 billion of revenue, Meta turned to the bond market to fund its AI build-out, and Apple guided its gross margin down to 45-46% from 47.9% as memory chip prices rose.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The Iran war and the Hormuz closure have held Brent crude above $100. Under US pressure, Ukraine paused its drone strikes on Russian refineries in mid-October, and the first Russian diesel tanker from Trump's deal with Putin to lower fuel prices is headed for New York, though it won't arrive before the Midterms.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: European gas passed €100 per megawatt hour in October, its highest since 2022, as the Iran war reached the region's gas supply. Strikes cut Iran's gas capacity by a fifth, Qatar agreed to import up to 4 million tons of US gas a year, and the Qatari carrier Al Mayeda was hit in the Gulf.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: The fortnight's news carried the Hormuz crisis lifting Aramco's third-quarter profit and the ECB's Machado warning against softer capital requirements for banks, but none of it is about American stocks or the options priced on them, and none of it accounts for this rise.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: The fortnight's Pakistani economic news was about domestic prices: imported gas for Punjab and Sindh rose with October crude, cooking gas sold at double the official rate, and flour stayed dear though wheat had fallen. None of it accounts for the rupee's slight firming against the dollar.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: None of the fortnight's Nigerian news explains the rate. Tinubu opened his re-election bid with petrol at about 1,400 naira a litre, then sought $20.5 billion and €1.04 billion in foreign loans. OPay raised $304 million in a New York listing, and suspected Ebola cases surfaced in the northeast.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: The fortnight in Cairo was shaped by the Iran war: Hormuz shipping stayed shut under a US blockade, and parliament voted behind closed doors to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia. None of the reporting ties those events to the pound or names another cause for its slide.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: Ankara's fortnight was diplomatic: it submitted the Makkah defence pact binding it to defend Riyadh, hosted Iran mediators in Istanbul, joined four states demanding Hormuz reopen, and offered to help restore Ukraine's grain corridor. None of it bears on the lira's price.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: Protests disrupted garment factories for a third day as workers demanded 30,000 taka a month, up from 12,500, and the government formed a wage board in response. Nothing reported ties that dispute, or anything else in the news here, to the exchange rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: The period's news from Jakarta was Indonesia cutting gas exports to Singapore, the Badr defence pact with Qatar, Turkiye and Pakistan, new stock market transparency measures and October inflation easing to 3.23%. None of it explains the exchange rate.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: Lebanon's news this fortnight was of Israeli forces bulldozing olive groves at Kfarshouba, and of Palestinian refugees in the Beddawi camp in Tripoli squeezed by high energy prices and inflation. None of it accounts for the pound's price.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan's climb pulled the People's Bank of China into the open: it set the fixing weaker at 6.7146 to slow the rise, then lifted the forex deposit reserve ratio from 4% to 6% from 15 November, locking up banks' dollars onshore to shield exporters from a currency up more than 9% since the start of last year.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: The RBI stepped into the market: likely central-bank dollar sales lifted the rupee to 95.02. It was defending the currency while a war pushed fuel prices up across Asia and made the oil India buys dearer.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: Lula's re-election over Flávio Bolsonaro, the market's pick, set off the slide: real futures fell 10% on fears of a wider fiscal deficit, and companies had already moved cash into dollar stablecoins. Economists in the Focus survey then raised their 2027 inflation forecast to 4.76% from 4.34%, pricing a fourth Lula term's spending against the Selic.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: Inflation of 3.62% in early October ran above forecasts, the one recent report from Mexico that bears on its currency, but it does not account for the peso's slide.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: Two forces pulled on the rate. The Iran war pushed European gas past €100 per megawatt hour, an import bill the euro area must pay. Meanwhile forecasters raised euro zone inflation to 3.0%, and the Bundesbank's Nagel called a third ECB hike this year almost inevitable. Lagarde steps down in February, and governments must nominate her successor by Friday.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen gained twice as money looked for shelter. Doubts about the AI boom lifted it to a one-month high of 156.28 per dollar. Then, as election returns pointed to a Democratic Congress, the dollar had its worst day in a month in Asian trading, with the yen up 0.7% and the Swiss franc almost 1%.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: Moscow held its key rate at 14%, keeping the return on holding rubles high. Diplomacy ran alongside it: Witkoff met Putin as Trump pressed Ukraine to cut a deal, and US-mediated talks between Ukraine and Russia were fixed for 10 November in Abu Dhabi.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: Washington suspended South Africa from duty-free access under the African Growth and Opportunity Act, which carried $1.7 billion of exports in 2025, a day before the country voted in its local government election. Both landed at the window's end; nothing earlier in it explains the rand's path.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: The weakest stretch followed the Binance heist. The FBI blamed North Korea's TraderTraitor for the $6.3 billion theft, and once withdrawals reopened customers pulled a net $4.72 billion while the promised proof-of-reserves report had still not appeared. On top of that, US bitcoin ETFs lost $399 million in a day.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: The low came as Binance froze funds after a $6.3 billion theft the FBI blames on North Korea's TraderTraitor. Withdrawals reopened and customers pulled a net $3.64 billion. Days earlier, the US Senate fell short of the 60 votes the Clarity Act needed, and the bill stalled.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: Gold slid as the war pushed oil up: the World Bank expects global oil supply to fall 5.2% in 2026, and dearer fuel kept the Fed talking higher for longer, bad news for a metal that pays no interest. Its 3.6% weekly fall in October was the worst since June; softer oil and dip buyers have since steadied it.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is the page readers land on when the technology itself, rather than one company or product, becomes the question.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Nothing here dates from the mid-October peak. The weeks after it were about the bill: Alphabet's capex jumped 114% to $51.4 billion in one quarter, Microsoft offered 60,000 buyouts while forecasting $175 billion in capital spending, and Anthropic's prospectus showed 7 co-founders holding 50.1% of the votes.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: Putin met Trump's envoy Witkoff, and Ukrainian and Russian officials meet in Abu Dhabi on 10 November with Washington mediating and Europe kept out of the room. Ukrainian drones, meanwhile, forced Yandex to move its 3 main supercomputers underground. None of this explains the early-October peak.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: On the same day the US struck Qeshm Island, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said 3 tankers had hit mines in the strait, and Tehran set five conditions for a ceasefire, among them recognition of its sovereignty over Hormuz. That came a day after Iran cut its offer to reopen the strait from 7 days to 2.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: The UN maritime agency counts 123 attacks on ships near Hormuz, and Iran now ties even a two-day reopening of the strait to the US lifting its blockade. Its Revolutionary Guards claim three tankers hit mines on 'unauthorized' routes, an unconfirmed assertion of which lanes are legal, after Qatar's LNG carrier Al Mayeda was struck.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: The war between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia was fought over land targets: missiles at Saudi oil sites and a pipeline, Saudi strikes on Yemen, attacks in Aden. None of it was aimed at ships. China and Djibouti backed free navigation in the Red Sea, but nothing reported accounts for the traffic through the strait.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: The fortnight's news around the Red Sea was diplomatic rather than physical. China and Djibouti backed free navigation in the Red Sea, Burhan offered Russia a Red Sea economic zone, and 14 Indian nationals were confirmed safe after a yacht attack off Yemen. None of it accounts for the canal's traffic.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The news around these waters in the fortnight was about other routes. Saudi Arabia will store crude in Singapore's Jurong caverns from 2027, Indonesia cut gas exports to Singapore, and limpet mines and fires hit tankers in Hormuz after the latest reading here. None of it accounts for traffic through Malacca itself.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: None of the fortnight's reporting accounts for the fall in transits, and calm seas rule out weather. The nearest event came after the data ends: Taiwan's map showed 53 Chinese ships around the island, 34 of them warships. The period's other big China stories, the Tibet earthquake and Kim Jong Un's visit, do not touch the strait.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Drones sank two cargo ships near the Black Sea's western shore: the Khoryv off Constanța, killing one sailor, and the Contship Jet off Bulgaria, whose 18 crew survived. Romania blamed Russia. Erdoğan then backed restoring Ukraine's grain corridor, and Rubio floated a Black Sea ceasefire. None of it accounts for the mid-October trough.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news touched shipping through the strait. The nearest stories were Italy and Spain lifting border checks after over 70,000 people entered Ceuta, and Libya's eastern parliament backing Turkey's 2019 maritime deal. Neither accounts for the traffic.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The fortnight's tanker news ran on other routes: limpet mines and fires aboard tankers in Hormuz, and Russian diesel sailing from Primorsk to New York. Neither passes the Cape of Good Hope, and none of it accounts for the traffic here.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: The fortnight's Black Sea shipping news was elsewhere: Erdoğan agreed to help restore Ukraine's grain corridor, and Rubio floated a limited Black Sea ceasefire ahead of Trump-Putin contact. Neither touches traffic through this strait, and nothing in the reporting accounts for it.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The fortnight's news from Türkiye was diplomatic, not financial: Ankara submitted the Makkah defence pact that would bind it to defend Riyadh, Istanbul hosted foreign ministers on the Iran war, and Erdoğan backed restoring Ukraine's grain corridor. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The fortnight's news from Malaysia was a 2027 budget that kept fiscal consolidation going, Binance in talks for a licence after a five-year absence, and a Tanaka plant that will recover gold from chip-factory scrap. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: Indonesia cut gas supplies to Singapore, October inflation eased slightly to 3.23%, and the government announced new measures to improve stock market transparency. None of it accounts for a fall this deep.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Tech stocks led the fall on AI worries, the same doubts that pushed money into the yen as a safe haven in late October. A stronger yen shrinks what exporters' overseas earnings are worth at home, and it climbed another 0.7% against the dollar as US midterm returns pointed to a Democratic Congress.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The slide came as investors repriced the AI trade: Contemporary Amperex fell 15% despite a 21.2 billion yuan quarterly profit, and China's blue-chip index posted a record 11 straight weekly losses. Third-quarter results split the market, tech profit up 140% while property lost 53.2 billion yuan, and new export orders fell to 48.7 in October.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: SK hynix shelved a Solidigm listing worth up to $15 billion. Seoul's military said North Korea had laid 960,000 border mines, and howitzers were later aimed south from Kaepung. South Korea's economy grew 1% last quarter, 3x the forecast. None of this accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: Jio Platforms' listing, India's largest IPO, filled in 100 minutes and debuted above its issue price, leaving Ambani owning India's two most valued firms. The RBI sold dollars to shore up the rupee against oil prices, and carmakers stocked dealers for the festive season; none of it is shown driving the index itself.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Indonesia cut gas supplies to Singapore, where gas generates up to 95% of the electricity, citing domestic energy needs, and Singapore's top envoy went to Jakarta to talk. Across the region, Japan's Nikkei slumped 3% as tech stocks tumbled on AI worries. None of the reporting ties either story to the index's banks or property firms.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's reporting on Taiwan was about security and weather: Taipei tracked 53 Chinese ships, 34 of them warships, in a wide sweep of its waters, and Typhoon Champi knocked out power to thousands. None of it accounts for the slide in the index.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Australia went into its rate decision with a fifth hike expected as the inflation fight intensified. Oil prices slumped on the eve of the decision, and nearby Japan's Nikkei fell 3% as tech stocks tumbled on AI worries.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The fortnight's South African news was about trade and the state rather than listed companies: Washington suspended South Africa from AGOA duty-free access, which carried $1.7 billion of exports in 2025, and the budget cut the fuel levy until January 2027. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: Lula overturned a first-round deficit to beat the market's pick in the runoff, and real futures fell 10% as markets priced a fourth term's spending. With inflation already through the target ceiling at 4.62%, economists raised their 2027 forecast to 4.76% from 4.34% and lifted their forecasts for the Selic, the rate Brazilian borrowers pay.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: Mexico's inflation hit 3.62% in early October, above forecasts, and Pemex posted a $573 million loss even as oil prices surged. Neither accounts for the index's path over these weeks.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: The fortnight carried Trump trimming some 50% tariffs on Canadian goods before the midterms, a Montreal summit whose declaration left out Canada's associate EU membership, and a Conservative victory in British Columbia that boosted Carney's energy ambitions. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The slide ran through big tech's results: Amazon's AI spending pushed its 12-month cash burn to a record $42.4 billion, Intel lost 23% after hours despite beating revenue guidance, and Apple guided its gross margin down to 45-46% from 47.9%. AMD's 97% jump in data-center revenue was the exception.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: Its big lenders reported strong numbers: HSBC's pretax profit hit $9.6 billion, up 32%, and Barclays paid shareholders £500 million while cutting 5,000 jobs. Brent fell 8.55% on Iran diplomacy and the budget lifted Britain's tax burden to a record 38.6%, though no report links either to the index.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: Dearer money ran against a brighter German outlook. Nagel backed a third ECB rate hike this year in December, and loan obstacles now hit 7% of euro zone firms, yet Ifo expectations rose for a sixth month, to 91.6. Schaeffler's cut of 3,500 jobs, three quarters of them German, showed where the industrial squeeze lands.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Long-term French government yields rose from 4% in August to above 5%, so the state now borrows above its own companies, and the economy shrank 0.1% before Fitch cut its outlook. Cost-of-living protests drew 410,000 marchers on one Saturday and, by a third weekend of riots, more than 500 arrests.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: ASML, its heaviest weight, sold out of lithography tools, with customers already asking for machines in 2029 and 2030. Forecasters also raised euro zone inflation to 3.0% this year, putting an ECB rate hike back in debate, though none of the reporting ties either to the index's swings.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The fortnight's news from Spain was the Toledo train collision that killed at least 68 people, police clearing the Puerta del Sol housing camp and a 25,000-strong pension march in Madrid. None of it concerns the banks that weigh most in the index, and none of it accounts for the price.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The fortnight's main news for Milan's banks was the ECB clearing Intesa Sanpaolo to bid €32 billion for Monte dei Paschi, while ECB policymakers brought a rate hike debate into the open. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: None of the fortnight's Swiss news accounts for the climb: a bitcoin fund listed on SIX, Proton questioned staff over their AI use, and Nigeria evacuated an Ebola patient to Switzerland. At the end came Swiss inflation at its highest in almost three years, and a franc up almost 1% as US midterms weakened the dollar.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The fortnight's Swedish news was a wave of cyberattacks that drove supermarket freezers across Europe to 50°C, and Sweden's central bank reviving the e-krona debate. Neither touches the industrial and telecom companies this index is built from, and nothing else in the input explains its path.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: Israel's election left neither bloc able to reach 61 seats without Arab parties, so no coalition is obvious, and Trump then said $4 billion in Israel aid stops at year-end. Khamenei's order to answer any attack without geographic limits, after a record October of ship attacks near Hormuz, kept war risk over its defence and bank stocks.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Election day closed a midterm campaign fought over his Iran war, with diesel at a record $6.52 a gallon in September and 43 million Americans voting early. In its last days Trump said $4 billion in Israel aid stops at year-end and answered "no" on striking Iran after the vote, though Netanyahu pressed him to.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: The Federal Reserve held on Wednesday despite intensifying inflation, and markets now fully price a December hike. TD Securities expected 3 dissents against the hold, Warsh's muddled messaging revived credibility doubts, and higher-for-longer rates left Bank of America with $109 billion in unrealized bond losses.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: Gas above €100 per megawatt hour, driven by the Iran war, has pushed euro-area households to expect 3.1% inflation, and Panetta and the Bundesbank's Nagel now back a December hike, the third this year. The ECB held at its last meeting as Lagarde said she leaves on 7 February 2027; governments must nominate her successor by Friday.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: Silver's slide ran alongside gold's, which reached a one-year low as higher oil and US inflation data bolstered bets on a Fed hike, raising the cost of holding a metal that pays no interest. Dip buyers then arrested gold's slide, and traders turned to Iran talk prospects and the US midterms.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: The Fed left interest rates unchanged despite the inflation it faces, and within days higher oil and fresh US inflation data had gold traders betting on a Fed hike instead. None of the fortnight's reporting explains what pushed prices up.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: The strait is a war zone: the US is enforcing a blockade on Iran, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim tankers using "unauthorized" routes have hit mines, asserting that Tehran decides which lanes are legal. Iran offered a two-day reopening if the US lifts its blockade; the UN maritime agency counts 123 ship attacks near Hormuz.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: The Houthi attacks of these weeks hit land targets: Saudi oil sites, a pipeline, Aden, and Riyadh's airport, which they declared a military target as flights resumed. China and Djibouti backed free navigation in the Red Sea, but nothing reported explains why more container ships came through the strait.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: The Houthis' war with Saudi Arabia widened late in the window, with claimed strikes on Saudi oil sites, attacks in Aden and a threat against Riyadh's airport, but none of the reporting concerns ships or the canal, and none of it accounts for the traffic.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The fortnight's reporting was about Hormuz: tankers striking mines, US strikes on Qeshm and Iran's shrinking reopening offer. All of it is dated after this series ends, and none of it explains the fall in traffic through Gibraltar.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: After Witkoff met Putin, a Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire let an aid convoy into besieged Oleshky and evacuees returned to Ukraine. Talks now open in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, the first US-mediated round since February, and Europe will not be at the table.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.
xmr.recent: The fortnight's reporting near this subject was about ransomware: the FBI named SafePay among the most active gangs, with more than 600 victims since 2024, and a Nefilim and Hive operator was sentenced after a guilty plea. None of it accounts for the price.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Apple launched a touchscreen M6 MacBook Pro and iMac. John Ternus's first quarter as CEO then set a record on iPhone growth in India, but Apple guided gross margin to 45-46% from 47.9%. The AI build-out is bidding up DRAM and NAND, so there will be no cheaper iPhones or MacBooks.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Alphabet's capital spending jumped 114% to $51.4 billion in one quarter, most of it on AI, enough to turn its free cash flow negative while search fell short of forecasts. The results landed in a week when tech earnings deflated AI enthusiasm across the sector. A fortnight earlier, on 16 October, Google had softened its Gmail ad-targeting promise.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: Amazon's latest earnings put its 12-month cash burn at a record $42.4 billion, as spending on AI infrastructure outran the cash its business brings in. The shares fell on the release, alongside other tech companies whose results raised the same question about what all that AI spending returns.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Microsoft offered buyouts to 60,000 employees to contain costs while forecasting $175 billion in capital spending this year, and Kaspersky found the BlackX bootkit infecting fully patched Windows machines by getting past Secure Boot. Neither story accounts for the share's swings.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: SpaceX has borrowed $40 billion for GPUs, mostly callable debt, and Pimco took $4 billion of the package. In Ukraine, drones lost Starshield links above 160 km/h for 10 days, Kyiv now plans its own satellites, and the Pentagon inspector general declined a nine-senator probe. A NASA adviser cites 22 refuelling flights for Artemis IV.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: New Mexico fined Meta $25 billion over the Cambridge Analytica scandal, and AI spending left the company $2.12 billion cash-negative for the quarter. To pay for data centres it moved to sell $95bn of stock, its largest ever, with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom eyeing up to $5 billion of it, then readied a bond sale.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: Aramco's third-quarter profit rose 9% to $31.2 billion on a 35% higher average selling price, even as output fell with Hormuz closed. The East-West pipeline to the Red Sea lets it sell around the strait, and it has begun expanding that route. A Houthi drone strike near its Shaybah field sent Brent to $110.63.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla's Q3 net profit fell 43% to $787 million as margins shrank, but talk around the share turned to SpaceX: the two companies explored a merger, and Barclays called one a key part of the bull case. Tesla also joined Samsung in opposing new US tariffs on Vietnam.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung's quarterly results came out the same day as Alphabet's and rattled tech shares, and the company pulled its fridges and washing machines from sale in Hong Kong, ending home appliance sales there. In early November it joined Tesla in opposing new US tariffs on Vietnam.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.
co:amd.recent: Intel dragged down CPU rivals in late October as fears about AI spending rose. Then AMD forecast fourth-quarter sales above estimates on AI chip demand, after data-center revenue jumped 97% to $8.55 billion. Much of that rests on a few buyers: Meta, which eyes a $95 billion stock sale to fund its AI push, and OpenAI.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.
co:lilly.recent: Lilly joined Walmart in objecting to OKX-ICE tokenized versions of its shares, and Belgium refused to cover Mounjaro. Neither accounts for the climb in the price.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: The CBN granted JPMorgan approval-in-principle to set up a merchant bank in Nigeria, the first licensing step for a firm present in Lagos since 1961. A new unit of that size does not account for the share's fall over the window, and nothing else in the fortnight's news concerns the bank's own business.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: SK hynix cancelled a Solidigm listing worth up to $15 billion, at a time when its own record US listing was trading underwater. Five days later its shares led a rise in chipmakers ahead of a Fed decision and the company's earnings. Neither event explains the broader fall in the share price.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.
co:walmart.recent: Walmart joined Eli Lilly and 36 other companies in objecting to tokenized versions of their shares on OKX-ICE, part of a majority of issuers that opted out. Nothing reported over the fortnight about Walmart's own business accounts for the share price.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: Customers are already asking ASML for lithography tools to be delivered in 2029 and 2030, as advanced packaging for AI chips pushes demand past what it can build. That sold-out order book is the only news about the company's own business in the window, and it does not explain why the share fell.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.
ez-cpi.recent: Forecasters now see euro zone inflation averaging 3.0% this year, and the latest reading was reported as a three-year high. Neither report says what pushed prices up.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: The only Solana news in the fortnight concerned its security programme: 809 reports, many of them AI-generated spam, swamped a $1 million bug contest, so filing one now costs 1 SOL. That change does not account for the token's fall.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: Ripple won final approval for its own U.S. national trust bank, putting its $2.5 billion stablecoin under a federal regulator, without lifting the token. It fell with the market: altcoins slid as traders sheltered in bitcoin, $356 million in longs were liquidated as bitcoin broke below $80,000, and a Binance hack sent bitcoin and ether tumbling.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: Hyperliquid drew attention as the offshore venue where traders bet on Anthropic's initial public offering at 10-fold leverage, a market no regulated US exchange offers. That new contract does not by itself account for the token's price over the period.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: CoinDesk's market reports twice singled out ZEC for one-day jumps, of 11% and then 8%, while Bitcoin traded around $83,000 and later near $81,000 ahead of a Fed decision. Neither report gives a reason for the coin's own moves.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: The Bank of England is set to raise rates to 4% to quell inflation, after policymaker Greene said inflation risks were bigger than thought. Gas is behind much of that pressure: it explains £161 of a £180 rise in UK bills, and the inflation and borrowing data frame the chancellor's Budget challenge.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: Finance minister Katayama said Japan was shifting to a wage-driven inflation phase, the case for rates to keep rising, while Ueda answered that the 2% goal was not yet sustainably achieved. Strategists said the BOJ's signal on its inflation target supported the yen, and foreign issuers sold a record $16 billion of yen bonds.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The central bank spent the past weeks managing the yuan, not the price of credit. Beijing raised the forex deposit reserve requirement to curb the yuan's rally, a step that pulls as much as $24 billion in foreign currency out of banks, and the PBOC set a weaker fixing at 6.7146. Neither step touched the policy rate.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia's board held the key rate at its October meeting and named high inflation expectations as its concern. The ruble slowed after the decision. The bank credited rising export revenues with backing the ruble, and it has since bought roughly $150 mln of yuan on the domestic market with almost every settlement.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: Reports from these weeks described households across Southeast Asia scaling back weddings as inflation and an energy crisis took their toll, and a fragile truce between Cambodia and Thailand. None of them ties either strain to the index's decline.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The slide tracked Houthi attacks on Saudi soil: a drone strike at Shaybah, claimed hits on oil sites and the East-West pipeline, and Riyadh's airport shut. The rebound came as the defence minister held talks in Tehran and Aramco's $31.2 billion quarter showed Hormuz's closure paying the kingdom.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The fighting around Hormuz reached the Emirates' own coast in late October. Oil from tankers attacked by Iran closed beaches in 3 emirates, Ras Al Khaimah among them, and Al Gharbia's pipeline output fell from 250,000 to 60,000 tonnes. By early November Gulf producers were exporting crude at pre-war rates again.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Inflation hit 7.2% in September against a 2-4% target, and the central bank answered with a half-point rate rise, lifting borrowing costs for the domestic firms the index is built on. Oil topping $110 after a Houthi drone strike near Saudi Shaybah field fed the same imported inflation, and a weak peso compounded it.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: Meta was told to pay $25bn to New Mexico for misleading consumers, then reported a quarter that ended $2.12 billion cash-negative on AI spending. It followed with a planned $95bn stock sale, its largest ever, in new nonvoting shares that left an overhang on the existing stock, and a cross-border bond offering.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: Tencent previewed its Hunyuan Hy4 model, offered developers 2,000 free search calls a month and added phone remote control to WorkBuddy, and QuestMobile counted 143 million monthly users for its Lvpaopao short dramas in August. None of that news accounts for the fall in the share.

stocks:AMZN.standing: The world's largest online retailer and, through Amazon Web Services, the largest seller of rented computing power. The cloud arm earns most of the profit, so the share moves on data-centre demand more than on shopping.
stocks:AMZN.recent: Amazon's latest results showed its AI spending outrunning the cash the business brings in: its 12-month cash burn hit a record $42.4 billion. The figure landed in the same week that tech earnings deepened doubts about the payoff from AI, and investors priced Amazon's outlays as cost rather than growth.

stocks:SPCX.standing: The rocket and satellite company founded by Elon Musk. It launches most of the world's orbital payloads on reusable Falcon rockets and runs Starlink, the satellite internet network that supplies most of its revenue.
stocks:SPCX.recent: SpaceX's revenue doubled last quarter, but its AI capital spending tripled, with $16.4 billion going to AI infrastructure, and it has borrowed $40 billion for GPUs, mostly callable debt. Musk himself warned of a neocloud shakeout. Nothing reported directly ties any of this to the share price.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom eyed up to $5 billion of Meta's equity raise for AI data centres, and Huang gave his blessing to the Marvell-Lumentum deal. iFlytek said it trained Spark X2.6 without Nvidia, and Google's chip challenge lifted its cloud sales. None of it accounts for the share's fall.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Saudi Arabia, the Gulf kingdom that is the world's largest oil exporter and the guardian of Mecca and Medina. It counts how many people looked the country up, not what happened there.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: The Houthi war reached Saudi soil. Air defences intercepted 10 ballistic missiles fired at a pipeline, and the Houthis declared the Riyadh airport a military target as flights resumed. Egypt's parliament voted to defend Saudi Arabia, while the Saudi defence minister went to Tehran to meet Iran's president.

poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US, Russian and Chinese leaders meet together in person before 2027. A three-way meeting would put Beijing at the table on matters Washington and Moscow usually settle between themselves.
poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.recent: The month's diplomacy ran through Russia: Putin met Trump's envoy Witkoff, Trump pressed Ukraine to make a deal, and US-mediated talks between Ukrainian and Russian officials were fixed for Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November, with the Kremlin saying Europe would not be at the table. None of it involved Xi.

poly-ex-cuba-leader-raul-castro-in-us-cu.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Raúl Castro, Fidel's brother, Cuba's president from 2008 to 2018 and party chief until 2021, is in US custody by year's end. Traders bet on Washington getting him before an American court.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, earning most of its revenue from search and YouTube advertising, alongside Google Cloud and Waymo. Its share is a running bet on whether AI assistants strengthen or erode the search ad business.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Alphabet's quarterly results showed capital spending up 114% to $51.4 billion as it builds its own chips to challenge Nvidia in the cloud, enough to turn free cash flow negative. Search revenue missed as Google admitted AI search makes less money per query, and the miss dragged Wall Street down with it.

poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with strikes, mediation and the Red Sea shipping the war hangs over.
poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.recent: Riyadh opened a channel to Tehran: Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president, and Makkah pact allies moved from defence to diplomacy. The war kept going: a Houthi refinery strike claim lifted Brent, a drone was downed in the Mecca region, and Saudi strikes kept hitting Yemen, where 281,000 have been displaced since August.

poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a US-Iran agreement reached in 2026 has Iran hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium, the material at the centre of the nuclear dispute and of any settlement between the two.
poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.recent: Bets on a handover rose as Qatari-mediated talks opened in Doha and Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 2 days of a deal. They fell back when three days of talks produced no deal, a lawmaker said Iran's parliament would unanimously quit the nuclear treaty, and US strikes hit Qeshm Island.

stocks:300750.SZ.standing: Contemporary Amperex Technology, the Ningde company listed in Shenzhen and the world's largest maker of electric-vehicle batteries. Carmakers from Tesla to BYD's rivals buy its cells, so its share tracks the EV and grid-storage build-out.
stocks:300750.SZ.recent: Contemporary Amperex reported a quarterly profit of 21.2 billion yuan, and its shares still fell 15% as China's tech stocks repriced. The earnings did not shield the company from the wider selloff.

poly-will-deepseek-ipo-by-december-31-20.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if DeepSeek, the Hangzhou AI lab spun out of the hedge fund High-Flyer, lists its shares before 2028. A listing would open China's most closely watched AI lab to public shareholders.

poly-bank-of-mexico-decreases-interest-r.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Banco de México cuts its overnight rate by a quarter point after November. That rate sets borrowing costs across Mexico and the yield gap that draws foreign money into the peso.
poly-bank-of-mexico-decreases-interest-r.recent: The fortnight's news carried the Fed's hold in Washington and markets pricing a December Fed rate hike, but nothing on Banxico itself, so none of it accounts for what traders are paying on this contract.

poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Venezuela's authorities formally schedule a national election before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on a vote being called, not on one being held.
poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.recent: Venezuelans marched in Caracas on Thursday demanding that a presidential election date be set. That protest is the only news in the fortnight about a Venezuelan vote. Nothing reported since shows any response from the government, and none of it explains the later swings in the price.

poly-will-any-country-join-the-mecca-agr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if any further country formally joins the Mecca Agreement before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the pact widening beyond its founding signatories.

poly-cuban-regime-falls-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Cuba's communist government loses power before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, set against a one-party state that has outlasted decades of US sanctions.

poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Peter Obi, the former Anambra governor who ran third in 2023, wins Nigeria's presidency in 2027. Its price is what traders will pay on an opposition upset of the ruling APC.
poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.recent: Nigeria's campaign news centred on Tinubu, who launched his re-election bid in Kaduna with petrol at about 1,400 naira a litre, and on Microsoft pledging to load Nigeria's candidate list into its AI systems. Neither story concerns Peter Obi directly, and nothing reported in the window accounts for the bets on him.

poly-netanyahu-out-before-2027-684-719-2.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu stops being Israel's prime minister before 2027. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with coalition crises, court cases and election timing.

poly-sudan-civil-war-ceasefire-by-decemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces agree a ceasefire before 2026 ends. The war, fought since April 2023, has driven the world's largest displacement crisis.

poly-will-luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva-win-.standing: A Polymarket parlay that pays only if three separate things happen: Lula wins Brazil's presidency, Gadi Eisenkot becomes Israel's prime minister, and Democrats take the US Senate. If any one leg fails, it pays nothing.
poly-will-luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva-win-.recent: Israel's vote left neither bloc at 61 seats without Arab parties, after polls had put Eisenkot 8 to 10 points ahead of Netanyahu. Shin Bet then rejected Netanyahu's claim that Arab voters committed fraud. In Michigan's Senate race, Rogers' spokesperson Abigail Ronson turned out to be a registered Israeli foreign agent.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Pakistan, the nuclear-armed South Asian state of more than 240 million people. It shows when world events send people looking for the country's basics.
wiki-pakistan.recent: Army chief Asim Munir went to Tehran amid the US peace deal deadlock and was told no enriched nuclear material would leave Iran, while Türkiye sought parliament approval for a joint defence agreement with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. At home, diesel reached Rs400.67 a litre and retired officials warned against a constitutional amendment.

stocks:005930.KS.standing: South Korea's largest company and one of the world's biggest makers of memory chips, smartphones and displays. It carries so much weight in Seoul's stock market that its share price moves the national index with it.
stocks:005930.KS.recent: Samsung is pulling fridges and washing machines out of Hong Kong months after quitting the mainland Chinese appliance market, keeping TVs and phones as Chinese brands take white goods. The share answers to memory chips instead: that business lifted it about 8% in a week before Thursday's earnings selloff on the Kospi.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire by the end of November 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each round of talks and each wave of strikes.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: Witkoff's meeting with Putin and Trump's pressure on Kyiv to cut a deal produced talks rather than a truce: the first US-mediated Ukraine-Russia talks since February open in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, with Europe excluded. The only truce agreed, Melania Trump's four-hour window at Oleshky, covered an evacuation, not the front.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on talks, envoys and sanctions decisions.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: The late-October rise came as Trump's envoy Witkoff met Putin, Trump pressed Ukraine to cut a deal, and Russia freed Stephen Hubbard. Talks are next: the first US-mediated round since February opens in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, with Europe kept out of the room, while the only truce so far was a four-hour window to evacuate Oleshky.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Shares of the Cupertino maker of the iPhone, Mac and iPad, one of the world's most valuable listed companies. The iPhone earns most of its revenue, and its products are assembled largely in China on chips made in Taiwan.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Apple launched the M6 MacBook Pro and iMac, the Pro with a touchscreen, and John Ternus's first quarter as CEO set a record, with India driving iPhone growth. It also guided gross margin to 45-46%, down from 47.9%, as the AI build-out bids up DRAM and NAND, and said there would be no cheaper iPhones or MacBooks.

stocks:002236.SZ.standing: One of China's two largest makers of surveillance cameras and video systems, based in Hangzhou. US export blacklisting and an FCC equipment ban shut it out of American markets, so its sales lean on China and emerging markets.
stocks:002236.SZ.recent: The one item on Dahua's own business, a 2.63 billion yuan AI compute win, came after the fall rather than before it, and nothing in the input accounts for the decline itself.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if no senior American and Iranian officials meet before 2026 ends. The two governments have met at that level only rarely since 1979, so a meeting would break a long pattern.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Three days of Qatari-mediated talks in Doha ended without a deal. Tehran then set five conditions for any regional security arrangement and called the US ceasefire proposal insufficient. US strikes then hit Qeshm Island and Bandar Lengeh, after Netanyahu had pressed Trump to strike Iran once the midterms were over.

stocks:SNP.RO.standing: Romania's largest oil and gas producer, listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange and controlled by Austria's OMV, with the Romanian state as a minority holder. It develops the Black Sea's Neptun Deep gas field with Romgaz.

stocks:SNG.RO.standing: Romania's largest natural gas producer, majority-owned by the state and listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange. It owns half of Neptun Deep, the deep-water Black Sea gas project it is developing with OMV Petrom.

stocks:RDDT.standing: Shares of Reddit, the US forum built from thousands of user-run communities, listed on the New York Stock Exchange since 2024. It earns from advertising and from licensing its users' posts to AI companies as training data.
stocks:RDDT.recent: Reddit lost over 1 million weekly search referrals in October as AI answers stopped sending clicks, and Steve Huffman told shareholders the site is moving to logged-in-only access. The wall serves two ends at once: keeping AI scrapers out and selling its data to them, at the cost of the search visitors who arrived without an account.

stocks:RTX.standing: An American aerospace and defence group whose Raytheon unit builds missiles such as the Patriot, and whose Pratt & Whitney engines power airliners and fighters. Its share moves on defence budgets and jet-engine output.

stocks:ABBN.SW.standing: A Zurich-based maker of electrification and automation equipment: switchgear, motors, drives and the control systems that run plants and grids. Its orders track what industry and utilities spend on power infrastructure.

stocks:6954.T.standing: Fanuc Corporation is a Japanese maker of industrial robots and the numerical controllers that run machine tools. Its orders track how much factories worldwide spend on automation, especially carmakers and electronics makers.
stocks:6954.T.recent: Trump set a 180-day clock on foreign robot imports in Washington, the first step toward tariffs on the machines Fanuc sells into American factories. That decision came at the end of the window, and nothing in the input explains the share's earlier fall.

stocks:6506.T.standing: One of the world's largest makers of industrial robots, servo motors and drives, based in Kitakyushu and listed in Tokyo. Its orders are read as an early gauge of factory spending in China and beyond.
stocks:6506.T.recent: Trump set a 180-day clock on foreign robot imports, which bears directly on the robots this company ships into the American market. That move came after the slide, and nothing in the input explains the earlier fall.

stocks:INTC.standing: The American chipmaker that both designs processors and makes them in its own fabs, the largest US bid at leading-edge manufacturing. Its share price answers to Washington's industrial policy as much as to PC and server demand.
stocks:INTC.recent: Intel beat its revenue guidance and still lost 23% after hours, because its PC chip sales plunged. Friday's drop knocked $12B off the US government's stake. A week earlier the FCC granted Intel a waiver from the ban on foreign-made robots, after the company said no US-made robot fits its fabs.

stocks:CRCL.standing: The company behind USDC, the second-largest dollar stablecoin. It earns most of its revenue from interest on the reserves backing each token, so its shares move with US interest rates and demand for stablecoins.

stocks:ESLT.standing: Israel's largest listed defence contractor, based in Haifa, making drones, artillery, electronic systems and munitions. Its order book follows Israel's own wars and European rearmament, and its share price answers to that backlog.

stocks:GM.standing: The Detroit carmaker behind Chevrolet, GMC, Cadillac and Buick, and one of America's largest by sales. Its profits lean heavily on pickups and SUVs sold in North America, so its shares are exposed to US car demand and trade policy.
stocks:GM.recent: General Motors said it was still all-in on EVs and autonomy, and the day after this window closed it agreed to pay $220 million for selling drivers' Smart Driver data to insurers. Neither of these accounts for the rise in its share price.

stocks:4901.T.standing: The Tokyo-listed Japanese group that outlived the collapse of photographic film by moving into healthcare, semiconductor materials and imaging, in one of the best-known corporate reinventions in Japan.
